question: A sampler operates at \(f_s=8\) ksample/s. Find \(T_s\) and the time of sample \(n=6\), starting with \(n=0\) at \(t=0\).
A 10 mW signal experiences 20 dB power loss. Receiver noise power is 0.01 mW. Find received signal power and SNR in linear units and dB.
Sample \(x(t)=8\cos(200\pi t)\) at 150 sample/s. Write the sample sequence and identify its baseband alias.
Only \(x[0]=1\) V and \(x[1]=0.5\) V are nonzero. Using normalized sinc interpolation, find \(y(0)\), \(y(T_s)\) and \(y(T_s/2)\).
Flat-top samples \(x[0]=1\), \(x[1]=0.5\) and \(x[2]=-0.5\) V are spaced by \(T_s=1\) ms. Each rectangular hold lasts \(\tau=0.4\) ms. Write the output and state the values at 0.2, 0.6 and 1.2 ms.
A hold lasts 50 microseconds. Find its amplitude ratio relative to DC at 4 kHz, attenuation in dB and equalizer gain at that frequency.
A PWM system uses \(w=8+12x\) microseconds, where \(x\) is in volts. Recover the message from a measured width of 17 microseconds.
A PPM pulse begins 18 microseconds after the slot reference. With \(t_0=10\,\mu\)s and \(K_t=20\,\mu\)s/V, find the message voltage.
A PCM system samples at 8 ksample/s and uses 64 uniform levels over \([-2,2)\) V. Find bits/sample, quantization step, bit rate and ideal binary baseband minimum bandwidth. Ignore overhead.
Estimate the SQNR for a full-scale sinusoid and a 6-bit uniform quantizer, using the no-overload uniform-error approximation.
Encode index 6 using three bits.
For normalized input \(x=0.1\) and \(\mu=255\), calculate the mu-law compressor output. Apply the inverse without quantization and explain what changes when quantization is included.

An illustrative ADM rule starts at \(\Delta_0=0.1\) V with previous bit 0. After repeated consecutive bits, double the next step, capped at 0.4 V. After a change, halve it, floored at 0.05 V. For bits 1,1,1,0, give the step used for each bit and the next step.
Find the FDM width for three 4 kHz channels with two 1 kHz guards.

Use predictor \(\hat x[k]=\tilde x[k-1]\), initial reconstructed value zero, and nearest-multiple-of-0.25-V quantization of the prediction error, with no clipping. For input \((0.30,0.70,0.60)\) V, calculate prediction errors, quantized errors and reconstructed samples.

A DM system samples at five times the Nyquist rate of a 3 kHz message band. The step is 250 mV. Derive and calculate the largest amplitude of a 2 kHz sinusoid that satisfies the slope-tracking condition.

Four channels each supply 8-bit samples at 8 ksample/s. A frame carries one sample per channel and one framing bit. Find frame size, link rate, frame period, bit interval, payload efficiency and ideal baseband minimum bandwidth.
Equiprobable OOK has OFF energy zero and ON energy \(10\,\mu\)J. Find average energy per bit.
Find noncoherent orthogonal BFSK spacing at 25 kbit/s.

A BPSK constellation has coordinates \(\pm\sqrt{E_b}\) with \(E_b=4\) in normalized energy units. Bit 1 uses the positive point. For received statistics \((0.8,-0.3,0.1,-1.2)\), give decisions and minimum point separation.

At \(R_b=20\) kbit/s, find BPSK bandwidth with raised-cosine roll-off 0.25, rectangular BPSK null-to-null width, and rectangular BFSK outer-first-null span with 20 kHz tone separation. Explain why the answers differ.
Find phase spacing for 16-PSK.
Use QPSK labels \(00,01,11,10\) at phases \(45,135,225,315\) degrees. With \(E_s=2\), map the bit stream 00111001 to phases and I/Q points. At 120 kbit/s find symbol rate and period.
Square 16-QAM uses axis levels \(-3,-1,1,3\), labelled \(00,01,11,10\). All points are equiprobable and I bits come first. Find average symbol energy, detect \((2.6,-0.7)\) and give its bits.
A 64-QAM system has \(E_b/N_0=12\) dB and raised-cosine roll-off 0.5. Find \(E_s/N_0\) in linear units and dB, and spectral efficiency.
Find MSK tones for \(f_c\) = 300 kHz and deviation=20 kHz.
Encode information bits 10110 with \(d_k=b_k\oplus d_{k-1}\) and initial state \(d_{-1}=0\). Then decode to verify every bit.
Design noncoherent orthogonal 8-FSK at 30 kbit/s using rectangular symbol pulses and lowest tone 100 kHz. Find symbol rate, duration, tone spacing, tone set and outer-first-null span.
At linear \(E_b/N_0=4\), compare coherent BPSK, coherent orthogonal BFSK, differential DBPSK and noncoherent orthogonal BFSK. Use \(Q(2)=0.02275\) and \(Q(\sqrt8)=0.002339\).
A matched filter receives a known signal in AWGN with \(E/N_0=3\) in linear units. Find its maximum output SNR.
Derive coherent BPSK BER for equal priors, points \(\pm\sqrt{E_b}\) and projected noise variance \(N_0/2\). Evaluate it at \(E_b/N_0=6\) dB. Use \(Q(2.8217)\approx0.002388\).
Estimate the high-SNR SER and Gray BER of coherent 8-PSK at \(E_b/N_0=12\) dB. Use \(Q(3.7318)\approx9.507\times10^{-5}\). State the approximation involved.
